paper.title: Online SuBmodular + SuPermodular (BP) Maximization with Bandit Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Interactive BP / weakly submodular maximization with monolithic feedback (GP contextual bandit)
unmapped: At each round one of m set functions h_q (index u_t revealed, with context phi_q) arrives; the learner picks one item from a finite ground set V, which is added to a growing per-context set; the reward is the noisy marginal gain h_q(v|S). Rewards therefore depend on the learner's past actions (state = accumulated set), observed as part of the context.
Regret is alpha-regret against alpha times the optimal set of size T_q for each context, with alpha determined by curvatures (BP) or submodularity ratio/generalized curvature (WS).
Marginal-gain function Delta(phi,S,v) lies in an RKHS with norm bound B; bounds stated through effective dimension d_eff(lambda,T).
settings.definition_quote: The optimizer encounters one of $m$ set functions from the set $\{h_1 \ldots h_m \}$ each defined over the finite ground set $V$... Monolithic Feedback: The optimizer receives $y_\tvar$ with $y_\tvar = h_{u_\tvar} (v_\tvar| S_{t_{u_\tvar}, u_\tvar}) + \epsilon_\tvar$.

settings.name_in_paper: Interactive BP maximization with separate feedback
unmapped: Separate feedback: noisy marginal gains of the submodular part f and supermodular part g are observed separately for the chosen item.
The learner knows the number of items T_q for each context (Assumption 2c) and, for Theorem 2, the modular lower bound l_{q,1} (Assumption 2a).
Rewards depend on the learner's accumulated per-context set (state observed as context).
Regret is alpha-regret with alpha = min{1 - kappa_f/e, 1 - kappa^g}.
settings.definition_quote: Separate Feedback: In the BP case, pair $(y_{f, \tvar},y_{g, \tvar})$ may be available with $y_{f, \tvar} = f_{u_\tvar} (v_\tvar| S_{t_{u_\tvar}, u_\tvar}) + \epsilon_\tvar/2$ and $y_{g, \tvar} = g_{u_\tvar} (v_\tvar| S_{t_{u_\tvar}, u_\tvar}) + \epsilon_\tvar/2$.

conditions: all h_q are BP functions (monotone submodular + monotone supermodular, MNN)
Delta lies in RKHS with norm <= B (Assumption 1)
tuning: beta_t = sqrt(lambda) B + sqrt(4 log T + log(e + e t/lambda) d_eff)

source.label: thm:bp_regret_bound
source.quote: Let Assumption~\ref{ass:rkhs} hold and assume that $\epsilon_\tvar$ are i.i.d centered sub-Gaussian (i.e., light tailed) noise. Then MNN-UCB (Algorithm~\ref{alg:smucb}) obtains the following regret: (a) When all $h_q$ are BP functions, we have that $\mathbb{E} [\mathcal{R}_{\text{BP}}(\Tvar)] \leq O\left(\sqrt{\Tvar} \left(B \sqrt{\lambda \deff} + \deff\right) \right)$

results.notes: B (RKHS norm bound) mapped to S. Comparator is alpha times the optimal set per context; best_policy chosen as the closest fit. Proof reduces to Zenati et al. 2022 Theorem 4.1.

conditions: all h_q are weakly submodular MNN functions with submodularity ratio gamma_q and generalized curvature zeta_q
Delta lies in RKHS with norm <= B (Assumption 1)
tuning: beta_t = sqrt(lambda) B + sqrt(4 log T + log(e + e t/lambda) d_eff)

source.label: thm:bp_regret_bound
source.quote: (b) When all $h_q$ are WS functions, we have that $\mathbb{E} [\mathcal{R}_{\text{WS}}(\Tvar)] \leq O\left(\sqrt{\Tvar} \left(B \sqrt{\lambda \deff} + \deff\right) \right)$

conditions: Assumption 2: modular lower bound l_{q,1} known, separate f/g feedback oracles, T_q known

source.label: thm:bp_regret_bound_dist_strong
source.quote: Let Assumptions~\ref{ass:rkhs} and \ref{ass:separate} hold and assume that $\epsilon_\tvar$ are i.i.d centered sub-Gaussian noise. Then, when all $h_q$ are BP functions, Algorithm~\ref{alg:mnnucb_dist} yields \[ \mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}_{\text{BP}, 2} (\Tvar)] \leq O\left(\sqrt{\Tvar} \left(B \sqrt{\lambda \deff} + \deff\right) \right) \]

results.notes: Stronger alpha than Theorem 1(a) thanks to separate feedback.

conditions: Assumption 1, Assumption 2b (separate oracles) and 2c (T_q known); l_{q,1} not required

source.label: prop:bp_regret_bound_dist_weaker
source.quote: Let Assumption~\ref{ass:rkhs} and \ref{assump:1.2} and \ref{assump:1.3} hold. Additionally, let the conditions on $\epsilon_\tvar$ hold as in Theorem~\ref{thm:bp_regret_bound_dist_strong}. Then Algorithm~\ref{alg:mnnucb_dist} with the modification above yields $\mathbb{E} [\mathcal{R}_{\text{BP, 3}} (\Tvar)] \leq O\left(\sqrt{\Tvar} \left(B \sqrt{\lambda \deff} + \deff\right) \right)$

results.notes: Modified MNN-UCB-Separate variant not requiring knowledge of l_{q,1}.
